references.text: Jesus uses the same image of the lamp in the Sermon on the Mount: "Nor does anyone light a lamp and put it under a bowl. They set it on a stand, so that it gives light to all in the house" ([ref:Matt 5:15|Matthew 5:15]). This is a close parallel where the lamp on the stand symbolizes that the light must not be hidden.

Mark has a parallel to this statement: "Does a lamp come in to be put under a bowl or under a bed? Is it not to be set on a lampstand?" ([ref:Mark 4:21|Mark 4:21]). The same image is used to show that the light must be visible to all.

Luke also uses this image earlier: "No one who lights a lamp hides it under a bowl or puts it under a bed. They set it on a stand, so that those who come in may see the light" ([ref:Luk 8:16|Luke 8:16]). Almost identical wording, with the same expression about "those who come in" (οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι) seeing the light.

The following verses ([ref:Luk 11:34-36|Luke 11:34-36]) expand on the theme of light by speaking of the eye as the lamp of the body. The context shows that the outer lamp in verse 33 points to the inner light – if the whole body is full of light, everything will be illuminated.

Jesus says, "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life" ([ref:Joh 8:12|John 8:12]). The image of the light being placed so that all may see it points to Jesus himself as the visible light for the world.

The prologue of John describes that "in him was life, and the life was the light of people. The light shines in the darkness" ([ref:Joh 1:4-5|John 1:4-5]). The light shining for all connects to the lamp metaphor in Luke 11:33 about the light not being hidden.

Isaiah prophesies: "Arise, shine! For your light has come ... Nations shall walk by your light" ([ref:Jes 60:1-3|Isaiah 60:1-3]). The theme of light being placed so that people can see it and come to it is an Old Testament background for Jesus' words.

Just before the lamp statement in the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says, "You are the light of the world! A city built on a hill cannot be hidden" ([ref:Matt 5:14|Matthew 5:14]). The same basic idea as in Luke 11:33 – the light and testimony are meant to be visible to all.

Paul urges the Philippians to "shine like stars in the world" and hold fast to the word of life ([ref:Fil 2:15-16|Philippians 2:15-16]). This reflects the same principle as in Jesus' parable of the lamp: believers are to let their light shine visibly for all.
